6. DECISION MATRIX: WHICH ERROR PATTERN TO USE
===============================================

Use crate::error::Result (BivvyError):
✓ Core business logic (config loading, step execution)
✓ When you want domain-specific error variants
✓ When error needs contextual information (path, step name)
✓ When caller needs to handle specific error types differently
✓ When building error messages for end users

Use anyhow::Result:
✓ Utility/helper code that's not domain-critical
✓ When you don't need to distinguish error types
✓ When wrapping multiple sources of errors
✓ When error handling is "fail fast" with simple reporting
✓ When code is deeply nested (?)operator is ergonomic

Use Box<dyn std::error::Error>:
✓ Integration/end-to-end tests only (assert_cmd requirement)
✓ NOT recommended for production code

NO custom error enums (besides BivvyError):
- Keep error types centralized in src/error.rs
- Use BivvyError::Other(anyhow::Error) for ad-hoc errors

6. DECISION MATRIX: WHICH ERROR PATTERN TO USE
===============================================

Use crate::error::Result (BivvyError):
✓ Core business logic (config loading, step execution)
✓ When you want domain-specific error variants
✓ When error needs contextual information (path, step name)
✓ When caller needs to handle specific error types differently
✓ When building error messages for end users

Use anyhow::Result:
✓ Utility/helper code that's not domain-critical
✓ When you don't need to distinguish error types
✓ When wrapping multiple sources of errors
✓ When error handling is "fail fast" with simple reporting
✓ When code is deeply nested (?)operator is ergonomic

Use Box<dyn std::error::Error>:
✓ Integration/end-to-end tests only (assert_cmd requirement)
✓ NOT recommended for production code

NO custom error enums (besides BivvyError):
- Keep error types centralized in src/error.rs
- Use BivvyError::Other(anyhow::Error) for ad-hoc errors

=====================

Location: /src/error.rs (single file, ~183 lines)

Core Error Type: BivvyError (thiserror-based enum)
- ConfigNotFound { path: PathBuf }
- ConfigParseError { path: PathBuf, message: String }
- ConfigValidationError { message: String }
- UnknownTemplate { name: String }
- CircularDependency { cycle: String }
- StepExecutionError { step: String, message: String }
- CommandFailed { command: String, code: Option<i32> }
- RequirementMissing { requirement: String, message: String }
- RequirementCheckFailed { requirement: String, message: String }
- ShellError { message: String }
- Io(std::io::Error) - #[from] for automatic conversion
- Other(anyhow::Error) - #[from] for wrapping unexpected errors

Result Type Alias: Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, BivvyError>

Features:
- Implements Display via #[error(...)] attributes
- All variants have contextual information
- Tests verify Display implementation for each variant
- Provides bridge between domain errors and anyhow via Other variant

6. DECISION MATRIX: WHICH ERROR PATTERN TO USE
===============================================

Use crate::error::Result (BivvyError):
✓ Core business logic (config loading, step execution)
✓ When you want domain-specific error variants
✓ When error needs contextual information (path, step name)
✓ When caller needs to handle specific error types differently
✓ When building error messages for end users

Use anyhow::Result:
✓ Utility/helper code that's not domain-critical
✓ When you don't need to distinguish error types
✓ When wrapping multiple sources of errors
✓ When error handling is "fail fast" with simple reporting
✓ When code is deeply nested (?)operator is ergonomic

Use Box<dyn std::error::Error>:
✓ Integration/end-to-end tests only (assert_cmd requirement)
✓ NOT recommended for production code

NO custom error enums (besides BivvyError):
- Keep error types centralized in src/error.rs
- Use BivvyError::Other(anyhow::Error) for ad-hoc errors
